title: Juniper and the Terminal
premise: Coral Quintana, the fourth clone of a woman murdered forty years ago, keeps the orbital beacon that decides which cryoship's sleepers wake when Earth's relay finally fails. When she finds her own name—Coral, not Coral-4—on the manifest of a ship that never launched, she uncovers the original's unfinished investigation into the beacon's true purpose: it was never a rescue system, but an inheritance dispute between two halves of humanity, coded to trust only the dead woman's judgment. Pursued by the consortium that killed the original and aided by Ilya Voss, the manifest ghost who turns out to be the original's secret partner in cryo, Coral must rewrite the beacon's selection logic before the relay dies. In the end she refuses both factions' claims, waking neither half by default but opening the choice to all sleepers equally—an act of belonging that costs her the beacon, her invisibility, and nearly her life, but gives her something the original never had: a future chosen rather than inherited.
about_author: E. M. Sandoval is a former radio astronomer who spent six years maintaining remote telemetry stations in the Atacama before turning to fiction. Their novels explore inheritance, identity, and the quiet violence of systems designed by people who never expected to be remembered.

chapters.title: The Beacon Keeps Its Own Hours
chapters.summary: Coral-4's POV. A day in her solitary routine aboard Relay Station Juniper: calibrations, log entries signed with a dead woman's name, the ritual of pretending to be someone she was decanted as. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the comfort of invisibility about to crack.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. During a manifest audit she finds the Meridian listed as launched—crewed by names including CORAL QUINTANA, no clone suffix—and a second unfamiliar name, Ilya Voss. The record predates her decanting. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: What the Original Left Running
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She decrypts the original's sealed personal partition, finding fragmented case files on her own murder and references to 'the Selection.' The consortium's legal AI pings the station for the first time in years. Emotional beat: dread dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: Ilya Answers
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. A voice responds from a derelict hulk at the system's edge—Ilya Voss, alive, unaged, claiming to have been in cold sleep since the murder. He knew the original; he mistakes Coral's voice for hers. Emotional beat: grief mistaken for recognition.

chapters.title: Two Halves of One Species
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ilya explains the beacon's hidden function: when Earth's relay dies, Juniper chooses which cryofleet wakes—the consortium's loyalists or the exiled dissenters. The original tried to make the choice herself. That's why she died. Emotional beat: the weight of an unwanted throne.

chapters.title: The Consortium Sends Regards
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. An 'inspection' vessel arrives with auditor Sef Adisa, courteous and lethal, probing how much of the original's partition Coral has accessed. She plays dumb; Sef doesn't believe dumb. Emotional beat: performance under pressure, first taste of being seen.

chapters.title: Inheritance Is a Kind of Evidence
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Working through the original's case files, Coral reconstructs the murder night from station logs—the killer used her own access codes. Whoever it was, they were family: another clone, or the original herself staging something. Emotional beat: intimacy with a corpse that is also yourself.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manifest
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya admits the Meridian never launched because he sabotaged it—he refused to let the original use his fleet as leverage. Their last fight was the night she died. His guilt has kept him frozen and hiding for forty years. Emotional beat: confession as absolution-seeking.

chapters.title: Sef Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sef reveals the consortium knows the relay is failing early—months, not years—and offers Coral a clean identity off-station if she hands over the original's partition. First real temptation: a life that isn't borrowed. Emotional beat: longing weaponized.

chapters.title: Decanting Day
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, the original Coral's POV, forty years prior. Her final day alive: coding the Selection override, fighting with Ilya, recording a message to 'whoever they grow next.' Emotional beat: tenderness toward a successor she'd never meet.

chapters.title: The Message Was Always Addressed to Me
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral finds the original's hidden message, keyed to open only for a clone who chose to look—not obey. It contains the Selection override and one instruction: don't decide like I did. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as permission.

chapters.title: Relay Decay
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The relay begins cascading failure ahead of schedule—Sef's inspection ship has been quietly accelerating it. Ilya's hulk starts drifting toward Juniper; the consortium moves to seize the beacon physically. Emotional beat: clock now audible in every scene.

chapters.title: Alliance of Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Coral and Ilya rendezvous via maintenance skiff. Awkward, charged partnership: he mourns her face, she resents being a memorial. They plan to broadcast the choice to both fleets before the consortium can lock the beacon. Emotional beat: two lonely people building trust from wreckage.

chapters.title: What Sef Wants
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef's motive surfaces: their sibling sleeps in the dissenters' fleet, and Sef joined the consortium to be positioned to save exactly one person. Sympathetic antagonist revealed. Emotional beat: duty and love wearing each other's clothes.

chapters.title: The Lockout
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Consortium forces board Juniper; Sef seizes the core but hesitates at the kill-switch. Coral triggers the station's ancient defense protocol—the original's last trick—and seals herself in the beacon chamber with hours of air. Emotional beat: courage that feels like suicide.

chapters.title: Negotiation at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral/Sef POVs. Through the chamber door, Coral and Sef negotiate across the divide: Sef wants their sibling woken; Coral offers everything except exclusivity. Ilya works outside to reroute power. Emotional beat: enemies discovering shared shape of grief.

chapters.title: The Choice Refused
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. With minutes left, Coral executes the override—not choosing either fleet, but unlocking the decision to every sleeper simultaneously: each pod votes, each person wakes themselves or waits. The consortium's binary collapses. Emotional beat: triumph that feels like surrender of control.

chapters.title: Waking Is a Riot
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Across both fleets, pods open in chaotic, unequal waves. Panic, joy, fistfights in corridors, strangers meeting after eighty years. Sef's sibling wakes and calls Sef's name. Emotional beat: humanity as beautiful mess, not order.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The consortium leadership, exposed by the broadcast logs—including proof of the original's murder ordered from within—is arrested by its own awakened security force. Sef testifies, trading immunity for truth. Emotional beat: justice arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: The Murderer's Name
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Final case file resolves: the original wasn't murdered by the consortium alone—a fifth clone, decanted secretly and discarded, executed her in jealous rage and died in the sabotage. Coral mourns a sister she never met. Emotional beat: grief completing the inheritance.

chapters.title: Juniper, Manned
chapters.summary: Coral and Ilya's POVs converging. The station fills with volunteers; the beacon becomes a lighthouse again, not a judge. Ilya asks to stay; Coral, for the first time, invites someone. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Signed, Coral Quintana
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She retires the old signature and signs a new log entry with her own hand: Coral Quintana, keeper of Juniper, first of her name. The relay holds; the fleets talk. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—an ending that is really a beginning.
